record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: In ageing science, do fundamental ageing processes exist and, if they do, how do those processes synchronize age-related changes and promote age-related diseases?

evidence.quote: Do fundamental ageing processes exist and if so, how do they synchronize ageing changes and promote age-related diseases?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Determine whether there exist fundamental biological processes of ageing — that is, a set of underlying mechanisms common to ageing organisms that drive the progressive functional decline observed with age. If such fundamental ageing processes exist, characterize how they coordinate and synchronize the diverse age-related changes that occur across different tissues and organ systems, and explain by what mechanisms they promote the onset and progression of age-related diseases (e.g., cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, cancer, metabolic dysfunction). A complete answer should (i) identify candidate fundamental processes (or rigorously argue for their nonexistence), (ii) provide a framework explaining their coupling to multi-system age-related phenotypes, and (iii) describe causal pathways linking these processes to specific age-related pathologies.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a foundational open question in biogerontology. While candidate frameworks such as the "hallmarks of ageing" (López-Otín et al., 2013, 2023) and "pillars of ageing" have been proposed, there is no consensus that fundamental ageing processes exist as unified drivers, nor a definitive mechanistic account of how they synchronize age-related changes and produce disease. The question remains actively debated in current ageing-research roadmaps.

status_evidence.title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe
status_evidence.snippet: Updated framework proposing twelve hallmarks of ageing as candidate fundamental processes, while noting many open questions about their interconnections and causal roles in disease.
status_evidence.claim: Candidate fundamental ageing processes have been proposed but their integration and causal links to age-related diseases remain open.
